mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to improved economic outlook.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over 3 months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market recovery, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE is above 7% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals rising inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to improved economic outlook.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, it signals a supply-side recession, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average and GDPC1 growth is negative.
